content: A module listed in the root registry without a canonical source path remains pending. Do not infer an implementation path, copy another project's maps or records, or write a missing child project as active merely because the root plan names it.
title: Pending modules are not active paths

content: An AgentHost/AgentRemote seam proves downstream decoupling, not multi-agent support. Current memory must distinguish the implemented neutral seam, the OpenCode concrete adaptor, and ACP adaptor family/selection as target work until a real adaptor and its verification evidence exist.
title: A seam is not adaptor coverage

content: Root memory must reference child architecture and governance boundaries without copying child maps, lifecycle records, Active, Protected, evidence, claims, mailboxes, journals, or historical hashes. Each child remains the canonical owner of its own truth.
title: Child truth is not root memory

content: appsdk verify, compile, static checks, or source-level tests do not prove a user-visible runtime installation, restart, or public-entrypoint result. Runtime claims require the built artifact, installed entrypoint, matching source identity, and real replay evidence.
title: Governance verification is not runtime proof

content: Routing, retry, provider selection, lifecycle, diagnostics, environment, snapshots, and governance state belong in typed control resources, error chains, records, or declared configuration. They must not be mixed into business request/response payloads or reconstructed from business data.
title: Control truth stays outside business payloads

content: When source contracts define a richer runtime architecture than the AppSDK function or mainline map, that mismatch is a governance gap to record and repair through the unique map owner. It is not evidence that the runtime architecture does not exist and not permission to invent symbols or claim full binding.
title: Runtime map gaps are owned work
